title: Choose the home-page composition
question: Which structure makes the game clearest for visitors while giving returning players the fastest route to their next action?

options.label: The Next Play
options.thesis: One unmistakable next action leads; the season record unfolds directly beneath it.
options.viewport: Guests see the game promise beside a three-step entry sheet; players see their rank, score, entry state, and next action in one joined board.
options.risk: The task-first hierarchy leaves less room for a broad marketing story.

options.label: Conference Command
options.lineage: arena stat desk split by East and West
options.thesis: League context frames the entry experience, with East and West acting as the page's organizing rails.
options.viewport: A central entry call is bracketed by live conference context, then resolves into the personal season ledger for signed-in players.
options.risk: Real standings can compete with the user's own prediction status if the balance is not exact.

options.label: Season Scorebook
options.thesis: The entire home page reads as one continuous score sheet from entry to rank.
options.viewport: A compact cover statement attaches directly to a live ledger; guests see how scoring works while players see their own row pinned in context.
options.risk: The continuous data rhythm can feel dense for a first-time visitor.
